#### Models
We follow closely the analysis of Wascher & Youngblood (2025) who modeled the Menzerath-Altmann law in crows. Note that a key difference in our random effect structure that we checked, was whether we should add `Nest` the individuals belong to as nested variable. The complete random structure would then be random intercepts for `Nest`, `Individual` nested within `Nest`, and `UniqueBout` nested within `Individual` (as indicated by `(1|Nest/Individual/UniqueBout)`. However, these models failed to converge, and we therefore follow Wascher & Youngblood (2025) in only including `Individual` and `UniqueBout` as nested random effects `(1|Individual/UniqueBout)`.

::: {.callout-note .callout-download collapse="true"}
# Key mixed regression models for assessing Menzerath-Altman law and assesment of age effects
```{r, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE}
library(lme4)
library(lmerTest)  # MUST BE LOADED BEFORE FITTING MODELS
library(dplyr)
library(equatiomatic)

# remove any rows with single element bouts (as these cannot be used for Menzerath modeling)
babdat <- babdat[babdat$BoutLength > 1, ]

# Using the same model as suggested by Wascher & Youngblood (2025)
parrotlet_menz_model <- lmer(scale(log(ElementDur)) ~ scale(log(BoutLength)) + (1|Individual/UniqueBout), data = babdat)

# store the residuals of the model (which we will regress against age later)
babdat$menz_resid <- resid(parrotlet_menz_model)

# add a model where we have age as a fixed effect
parrotlet_menz_model_age <- lmer(scale(log(ElementDur)) ~ scale(log(BoutLength)) + scale(Age) + (1|Individual/UniqueBout), data = babdat)

# assess interaction of age
parrotlet_menz_model_ageint <- lmer(scale(log(ElementDur)) ~ scale(log(BoutLength)) * scale(Age) + (1|Individual/UniqueBout), data = babdat)

# For LaTeX output (if using R Markdown)
equationmenz <- extract_eq(parrotlet_menz_model, use_coefs = TRUE)
equationmenz_age <- extract_eq(parrotlet_menz_model_age, use_coefs = TRUE)
equationmenz_ageint <- extract_eq(parrotlet_menz_model_ageint, use_coefs = TRUE)
```

# Plotting code for Menzerath's law models
```{r}
library(ggplot2)
library(cowplot)
library(lmerTest)

# Extract fixed effects coefficients
coef_menz <- fixef(parrotlet_menz_model)
coef_age <- fixef(parrotlet_menz_model_age)
coef_ageint <- fixef(parrotlet_menz_model_ageint)

# Create prediction data for plotting
pred_data <- data.frame(
  BoutLength = seq(min(babdat$BoutLength), 
                   max(babdat$BoutLength), 
                   length.out = 100)
)

# Basic Menzerath model plot
pred_data$pred_menz <- coef_menz[1] + 
  coef_menz[2] * scale(log(pred_data$BoutLength))

p1 <- ggplot(babdat, aes(x = scale(log(BoutLength)), 
                                  y = scale(log(ElementDurMedian)))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = data.frame(x = scale(log(pred_data$BoutLength)),
                              y = pred_data$pred_menz),
            aes(x = x, y = y), color = "#FD8D3C", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, 
           label = sprintf("y = %.3f + %.3fx", coef_menz[1], coef_menz[2]),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Scaled log(Bout Length)", 
       y = "Scaled log(Element Duration)",
       title = "Menzerath's Law: Basic Model") +
  my_theme()

# Age model plot
pred_data$pred_age <- coef_age[1] + 
  coef_age[2] * scale(log(pred_data$BoutLength))

p2 <- ggplot(babdat, aes(x = scale(log(BoutLength)), 
                                  y = scale(log(ElementDurMedian)))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8) +
  geom_line(data = data.frame(x = scale(log(pred_data$BoutLength)),
                              y = pred_data$pred_age),
            aes(x = x, y = y), color = "#FD8D3C", linewidth = 1) +
  annotate("text", x = Inf, y = Inf, 
           label = sprintf("y = %.3f + %.3fx + %.3f*Age", 
                          coef_age[1], coef_age[2], coef_age[3]),
           hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, size = 2.5) +
  labs(x = "Scaled log(Bout Length)", 
       y = "Scaled log(Element Duration)",
       title = "Menzerath's Law: With Age Effect") +
  my_theme()

# Create 8 age levels for subplots - use unique values
age_levels <- unique(quantile(babdat$Age, seq(0.05, 0.95, length.out = 9), na.rm = TRUE))
# Adjust number of bins based on actual unique age levels
n_levels <- length(age_levels)
# Create prediction data for each age level
pred_int <- expand.grid(
  BoutLength = seq(min(babdat$BoutLength), 
                   max(babdat$BoutLength), 
                   length.out = 100),
  Age = age_levels
)
pred_int$pred <- coef_ageint[1] + 
  coef_ageint[2] * scale(log(pred_int$BoutLength)) +
  coef_ageint[3] * scale(pred_int$Age) +
  coef_ageint[4] * scale(log(pred_int$BoutLength)) * scale(pred_int$Age)
# Create breaks for cutting - n_levels + 1 breaks creates n_levels bins
age_breaks <- seq(min(babdat$Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
                  max(babdat$Age, na.rm = TRUE), 
                  length.out = n_levels + 1)
# Assign age bins to raw data for faceting
babdat$age_bin <- cut(babdat$Age, 
                               breaks = age_breaks,
                               include.lowest = TRUE,
                               labels = paste("Age:", round(age_levels, 0)))
# Assign matching labels to prediction data
pred_int$age_bin <- factor(paste("Age:", round(pred_int$Age, 0)),
                           levels = paste("Age:", round(age_levels, 0)))
# Calculate slope for each age level
slopes <- data.frame(
  age_bin = factor(paste("Age:", round(age_levels, 0)),
                   levels = paste("Age:", round(age_levels, 0))),
  Age = age_levels,
  slope = coef_ageint[2] + coef_ageint[4] * scale(age_levels)
)
# Create color palette - adjust to actual number of levels
age_colors <- colorRampPalette(brewer.pal(9, "YlOrRd"))(n_levels)
# Create faceted plot
p3 <- ggplot(babdat, aes(x = scale(log(BoutLength)), 
                                  y = scale(log(ElementDur)))) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, size = 0.8, color = "grey50") +
  geom_line(data = pred_int,
            aes(x = scale(log(BoutLength)), y = pred, color = age_bin), 
            linewidth = 1.2) +
  geom_text(data = slopes, 
            aes(label = sprintf("β = %.3f", slope)),
            x = Inf, y = Inf, hjust = 1.1, vjust = 1.5, 
            size = 2.5, fontface = "italic", color = "black") +
  scale_color_manual(values = age_colors, guide = "none") +
  facet_wrap(~ age_bin, nrow = 2) +
  labs(x = "Scaled log(Bout Length)", 
       y = "Scaled log(Element Duration)",
       title = "Menzerath's Law: Development Across Age") +
  my_theme() +
  theme(
    strip.background = element_rect(fill = "grey90", color = "grey60"),
    strip.text = element_text(size = 8, face = "bold"),
    panel.spacing = unit(0.5, "lines")
  )
```

# General pattern Menzerath's law in babbling
```{r, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)
library(dplyr)

# Get coefficient summary from the basic model
sum_basic <- coef(summary(parrotlet_menz_model))

# Extract values for inline reporting
menz_slope <- sprintf("%.3f", sum_basic[2, "Estimate"])
menz_slope_se <- sprintf("%.3f", sum_basic[2, "Std. Error"])
menz_slope_t <- sprintf("%.2f", sum_basic[2, "t value"])
menz_slope_p <- ifelse(sum_basic[2, "Pr(>|t|)"] < 0.001, "< 0.001", 
                       sprintf("= %.3f", sum_basic[2, "Pr(>|t|)"]))

# Create basic Menzerath model coefficient table
menz_coef_table <- data.frame(
  Parameter = c("Intercept", "log(Bout Length)"),
  Estimate = c(sum_basic[1, "Estimate"], sum_basic[2, "Estimate"]),
  SE = c(sum_basic[1, "Std. Error"], sum_basic[2, "Std. Error"]),
  t_value = c(sum_basic[1, "t value"], sum_basic[2, "t value"]),
  p_value = c(sum_basic[1, "Pr(>|t|)"], sum_basic[2, "Pr(>|t|)"])
)

# Format p-values
menz_coef_table$p_formatted <- ifelse(menz_coef_table$p_value < 0.001, "< 0.001",
                                      sprintf("%.3f", menz_coef_table$p_value))
# Format other columns
menz_coef_table$Estimate <- sprintf("%.3f", menz_coef_table$Estimate)
menz_coef_table$SE <- sprintf("%.3f", menz_coef_table$SE)
menz_coef_table$t_value <- sprintf("%.2f", menz_coef_table$t_value)

```

(β = `r menz_slope`, SE = `r menz_slope_se`, p `r menz_slope_p`)

# Effect of Age on Menzerath's law
```{r, message =FALSE, warning =FALSE}
# model report
library(lme4)
library(dplyr)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

# ANOVA tests for model comparisons
anova_age <- anova(parrotlet_menz_model, parrotlet_menz_model_age)
anova_interaction <- anova(parrotlet_menz_model_age, parrotlet_menz_model_ageint)
anova_full <- anova(parrotlet_menz_model, parrotlet_menz_model_age, parrotlet_menz_model_ageint)

# Extract key statistics for inline reporting
age_chisq <- round(anova_age$Chisq[2], 2)
age_df <- anova_age$Df[2]
age_p <- round(anova_age$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2], 4)
age_p_formatted <- ifelse(age_p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", age_p))

int_chisq <- round(anova_interaction$Chisq[2], 2)
int_df <- anova_interaction$Df[2]
int_p <- round(anova_interaction$`Pr(>Chisq)`[2], 4)
int_p_formatted <- ifelse(int_p < 0.001, "< 0.001", paste("=", int_p))

# Get coefficient summaries with p-values
sum_basic <- summary(parrotlet_menz_model)$coefficients
sum_age <- summary(parrotlet_menz_model_age)$coefficients
sum_ageint <- summary(parrotlet_menz_model_ageint)$coefficients

# Create coefficient table
coef_table <- data.frame(
  Model = c("Basic", "", 
            "Age Effect", "", "",
            "Age Interaction", "", "", ""),
  Parameter = c("Intercept", "log(BoutLength)",
                "Intercept", "log(BoutLength)", "Age",
                "Intercept", "log(BoutLength)", "Age", "log(BoutLength) × Age"),
  Estimate = c(
    sum_basic[1, 1], sum_basic[2, 1],
    sum_age[1, 1], sum_age[2, 1], sum_age[3, 1],
    sum_ageint[1, 1], sum_ageint[2, 1], sum_ageint[3, 1], sum_ageint[4, 1]
  ),
  SE = c(
    sum_basic[1, 2], sum_basic[2, 2],
    sum_age[1, 2], sum_age[2, 2], sum_age[3, 2],
    sum_ageint[1, 2], sum_ageint[2, 2], sum_ageint[3, 2], sum_ageint[4, 2]
  ),
  t_value = c(
    sum_basic[1, 3], sum_basic[2, 3],
    sum_age[1, 3], sum_age[2, 3], sum_age[3, 3],
    sum_ageint[1, 3], sum_ageint[2, 3], sum_ageint[3, 3], sum_ageint[4, 3]
  ),
  p_value = c(
    sum_basic[1, 5], sum_basic[2, 5],
    sum_age[1, 5], sum_age[2, 5], sum_age[3, 5],
    sum_ageint[1, 5], sum_ageint[2, 5], sum_ageint[3, 5], sum_ageint[4, 5]
  )
)

# Format p-values
coef_table$p_formatted <- ifelse(coef_table$p_value < 0.001, "< 0.001",
                                 sprintf("%.3f", coef_table$p_value))

# Format other columns
coef_table$Estimate <- sprintf("%.3f", coef_table$Estimate)
coef_table$SE <- sprintf("%.3f", coef_table$SE)
coef_table$t_value <- sprintf("%.2f", coef_table$t_value)

# Create model comparison table
comparison_table <- data.frame(
  Comparison = c("Basic vs. Age Effect", "Age Effect vs. Age Interaction"),
  Chi_square = c(age_chisq, int_chisq),
  df = c(age_df, int_df),
  p_value = c(age_p_formatted, int_p_formatted)
)

# Print coefficient table
coef_table %>%
  select(Model, Parameter, Estimate, SE, t_value, p_formatted) %>%
  kable(format = "html", 
        caption = "Table 1. Fixed Effects Estimates for Menzerath Models",
        col.names = c("Model", "Parameter", "Estimate", "SE", "t-value", "p"),
        align = c("l", "l", "r", "r", "r", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE) %>%
  pack_rows("Basic Model", 1, 2) %>%
  pack_rows("Age Effect Model", 3, 5) %>%
  pack_rows("Age Interaction Model", 6, 9)

# Print comparison table
comparison_table %>%
  kable(format = "html",
        caption = "Table 2. Model Comparison Tests",
        col.names = c("Model Comparison", "χ²", "df", "p"),
        align = c("l", "r", "c", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```


Next we added Age as a fixed effect to the Menzerath model to assess whether age improves model fit. More importantly, we assessed whether the interaction between bout length and age further improved model fit.

Adding age as a fixed effect significantly improved model fit 
(χ² = `r age_chisq`, df = `r age_df`, p `r age_p_formatted`)

# The interaction between bout length and age further improved the model 
(χ² = `r int_chisq`, df = `r int_df`, p `r int_p_formatted`)




```{r, message =FALSE, warning =FALSE}

  kable(format = "html",
        caption = "Table 2. Model Comparison Tests",
        col.names = c("Model Comparison", "χ²", "df", "p"),
        align = c("l", "r", "c", "r")) %>%
  kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "hover", "condensed"),
                full_width = FALSE)
```


# Menzereth model squared residuals vs. Age

With increasing age there is a clear decrease in the squared residuals of the Menzerath model, indicating that older individuals become less variable in general and thereby deviate less from the trend line. This pattern reflects also can reflect that Age moderates the relation between bout length and element duration, as indicated by the significant interaction effect in the model including age as a moderator.

```{r, message =FALSE, warning =FALSE}
# get the average absolute residuals per individual per age
babdat$average_residuals <- ave(babdat$menz_resid^2, babdat$Age, FUN = mean)

# remove duplicates
babdat_individual_age <- babdat[!duplicated(paste0(babdat$Age)), ]

p5 <- ggplot(babdat_individual_age, aes(x = Age, y = average_residuals)) +
  geom_point(size=2) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "#FD8D3C", linewidth = 1) +
  labs(x = "Age",
       y = "Menzerath Model Squared Residuals (averaged per individual per age)",
       title = "Menzerath Model Residuals vs. Age") +
  my_theme()

p5
```
